evidence_summary: Effects Database explicitly identifies the Jax-USA FW-3 as manufactured in the United States by Applied Audio and places it inside the Applied FW-3 OEM line alongside Guild, Crown, Kadent, Atlantic, Lou Rose, Magnum, Nomad, and V-Jay.
Effects Database identifies the Atlantic FW-3 as U.S.-made by Applied Audio and notes that it shares the Applied FW-3 circuitry and layout, differing in cosmetic presentation.
Effects Database documents the Magnum FW-3 as a U.S.-made Applied Audio product within the FW-3 OEM series.

Effects Database identifies the Nomad Fuzz Wah as Applied Audio production and places it in the same FW-3 family. Nomad remains the marketed identity, while LIMMCO is treated separately as the distribution/house-brand context.
Effects Database identifies the V-Jay FW-3 as manufactured in the United States by Applied Audio and as part of the same FW-3 marketed family.
Effects Database explicitly identifies the Crown FW-3 as produced in the United States by Applied Audio and as a marketed state of the Applied FW-3.

The Guild FW-3 is independently documented as an Applied-built U.S. OEM model, with Effects Database listing the 1970-1978 catalog window and Catalinbread preserving the Applied/Guild historical relationship.
The Applied-branded FW-3 is the base U.S. production platform from which the listed OEM labels appear. The archive keeps the platform record distinct from each marketed identity.

Effects Database links Applied Banshee Wah to the Applied Wah Wah OEM family. Tone Machines notes that related Banshee fuzz products have unknown manufacturing dates, so broad family dating is not inherited here.

The Applied OEM index places Hohner WW-20 in the Applied Wah Wah family, but model-specific production evidence is thinner than for Guild VW-1 or the FW-3 variants. Kept below public-promotion threshold.
